# Capacity baseline (P0.9)

Every replay-corpus recording (`backend/python/tests/fixtures/journals/legacy/`) projected onto the P1 journal under the commit rules of REPORT §6.1.4. Model: `backend/python/tests/harness_replay/capacity.py`. See `SLO.md` for the gates these numbers feed.

## Assumptions

| Constant | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inline payload limit | 256 KB | REPORT §6.1.2 claim-check |
| Envelope bytes per event | 420 | §6.1.2 envelope, 24-char ids |
| Payload ref bytes | 120 | `{ref, hash, size}` |
| Raw provider copies per `model.response` | 1 | robustness #18 |
| Extra Mongo docs per commit | 4 | receipt, seq counter, run CAS, outbox |
| Model call latency | 3.0 s | assumed until the P1 load test |
| Tool batch latency | 0.5 s | assumed until the P1 load test |
| Code-mode gateway calls/s | 50 | assumed |
| Code-mode read outcomes per commit | 100 | robustness #23 |

Commit rules applied: admission (Node) and claim + spec pin (Node) are one commit each; `model.response` (with `model.request`, `usage.recorded`, `turn.started`) is its own commit before any dispatch; each `write`/`execute` intent is its own commit; `read` intents ride with their outcomes; all outcomes of a batch are one commit, or consecutive commits past 100 events (the journal's limit for one commit; a call's events stay together); a final answer carries `message.completed` and `run.completed` in its model commit; an interaction is a suspension commit (plus Node resolve and re-claim when the run continues).

## Commit and journal rate per worker at N concurrent runs

Commits/s = N × commits ÷ assumed run duration; journal growth = N × inline bytes ÷ duration. A worker at N runs in steady state.

| Profile | Metric | N=1 | N=4 | N=16 | N=64 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| corpus mean | commits/s | 0.6 | 2.5 | 10.0 | 40.1 |
| | journal MB/hour | 4.2 | 16.8 | 67.2 | 268.6 |
| busiest recording (`quick-ask-user-question`) | commits/s | 1.1 | 4.6 | 18.3 | 73.1 |
| | journal MB/hour | 5.8 | 23.1 | 92.2 | 369.0 |
| synthetic: code mode, 5,000 calls | commits/s | 0.5 | 2.1 | 8.5 | 33.8 |
| | journal MB/hour | 400.9 | 1,603.5 | 6,413.9 | 25,655.7 |

The per-session seq counter serializes commits within one session only (robustness #3); these rates are spread across N sessions. A single code-mode session commits at the rate in its N=1 column on one counter.

## One Node process (measured)

Node serves every admission, claim and commit on one thread. Measured on the PERF-C rig (PERFC-F1; MongoDB itself answers in a millisecond or two): a commit costs that thread about 4 ms, an admission about 9 ms and the commit that ends a run about 9 ms; with the claims, streams and logs of the same turns the thread is saturated at about 62 commits/s of the corpus turn. Requests that arrive in the same instant queue on it: k commits at once end about k × 4 ms later, so SLO #1's 100 ms leaves room for about 25 commits of one instant on one process, or 11 ending commits.

These per-request figures are PERF-C's derived ones; PERF-D and PERF-E measured them about twice as high on a loaded host (PERFD-F2), and stage 12 sets them from a quiet host.

**What is held per process and what is counted here (PERFD-F1, decided 2026-10-18).** Compose ships one Node process; Helm one per pod, scaled by its autoscaler on one core of CPU or on Node's event-loop utilization. SLO #1 and SLO #4 for sessions in step are held on one process (`commits-n16-instep`) whatever the topology: the rows below count how many processes a *rate* needs, which is a sizing figure, never a reason to restate a latency gate.

| Profile | Metric | N=1 | N=4 | N=16 | N=64 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| corpus mean | share of one Node process | 1% | 4% | 16% | 65% |
| | Node processes at saturation | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| busiest recording (`quick-ask-user-question`) | share of one Node process | 2% | 7% | 29% | 118% |
| | Node processes at saturation | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| synthetic: code mode, 5,000 calls | share of one Node process | 1% | 3% | 14% | 55% |
| | Node processes at saturation | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

Size for headroom, not for saturation: at the saturated rate every request waits behind the others (the overload profile `commits-n16-burst` measures that queue).
